analysis:
Examined the head excerpts of ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift (lines 552-1678) and the ProviderLoop+Preload.swift patch. The security-relevant changes are small and tighten model-selection and eviction controls.

1) Model-selection gate: autopilotAllowsModel is replaced by autopilotServesModel in handleLoadModelRequest (Preload.swift:30) and in ensureModelLoaded (ModelLoading.swift:207, visible in the patch only). The Autopilot-owned load escape is kept: autopilotCommandId must match the active command and its loadModelId. The gate still fails closed with model_not_selected. I could not see autopilotServesModel's definition, so I cannot confirm whether it is stricter or looser than autopilotAllowsModel. The head code shows no fail-open path, but the next pass should check that definition.

2) Eviction: evictableModelSlots (head 1299-1310) now also excludes autopilotHoldsModel, in addition to the existing pin, in-flight, local-reservation, unloading and MTP-retained checks. This narrows eviction. unloadModel(forEviction:) already rechecks the autopilot command, in-flight requests and reservations as the authoritative gate.

3) unloadModel now calls reconcileAutopilotPlacements() synchronously, immediately after the slot is removed (head 1146-1148) and before the later awaits. This closes a window where a reload could occur under a stale placement. It is a state-ordering fix and adds no new trust surface.

4) finishPreloadTask changes from private to internal. It is only reachable inside the module, which is a minor surface increase. It should be confirmed that its only callers are trusted test or autopilot code.

5) The load path is otherwise unchanged in the visible context. The weight-hash TOCTOU bracket (head 604-641) and the cache-eligible hash only for reusable SSD loads are intact and consistent with T-041 and T-012. The T-041 SSD cache gating and salt scoping are not touched. The coordinator-visible failure mapping (loadInferenceFailure) does not expose underlying errors.

No regressions against the threat model identified. The open question is the semantics of autopilotServesModel and autopilotHoldsModel, which are defined outside the supplied evidence.
